title: Unload a tray of soup from a serving pass and serve the bowl onto a placemat
instruction: Unload the tray from the pass without spilling the soup, leaving the tray lying flat on the table and the bowl of soup standing on the blue placemat.
context: Food runners take loaded trays off a kitchen pass, often from under a shelf, set them down and serve from them: the soup cannot be reached until the tray is drawn out, and tipping the tray on the way down spills it.
setup: A table in front of two arms (bases 61 cm apart), seen by one overhead camera and a camera on each wrist. Distances are measured forward from the line between the arm bases and sideways from the midpoint between them. (1) A fixed wooden serving pass on the centre line: a lower shelf, a block 12 cm deep (front to back), 24 cm wide and 12 cm tall with its front edge 25 cm forward; and an upper shelf 1 cm thick and 20 cm wide, from 27.5 to 41 cm forward, its underside 21 cm above the table, held up by a back panel at 40 to 41 cm. (2) A dark grey plastic serving tray, 36 cm wide (side to side) and 20 cm deep, with a 6 mm floor and rims 1.6 cm tall and 5 mm thick, 0.35 kg, loose, resting on the lower shelf centred 30 cm forward on the centre line; its left and right rims stick out past the pass. (3) A white ceramic soup bowl, inside 9 cm across and 5 cm deep (318 ml to the brim), with a flat handle 3.5 cm long, 2 cm tall and 8 mm thick sticking out to the right, 0.25 kg empty, standing in the middle of the tray under the upper shelf. (4) The soup: in a real trial, 150 ml (150 g) of room-temperature water tinted orange with food colouring, filling the bowl about 2.4 cm deep, 2.6 cm below its rim (it reaches the rim if the bowl tilts about 30 degrees). In simulation it is 15 orange plastic beads 8 mm across (1.5 g each), each standing for 10 ml of the soup, and the soup's remaining 127.5 g is added to the bowl's body (0.3775 kg), so the bowl with its soup weighs 0.40 kg, as in a real trial. (5) A round blue placemat 13 cm across, flat on the table, its centre 32 cm forward and 26 cm right of the centre line. The layout is the same in every trial, as in the screenshot.
scoring: Judged at the end of the trial, except the tipping rule, which covers the whole trial. 0.0 if the bowl is ever tipped 45 degrees or more, or ends tilted 15 degrees or more. Otherwise 1.0 with the bowl standing on the placemat (its centre within 4 cm of the placemat's centre), the tray lying flat on the table (tilted less than 10 degrees) and at most 10 ml of soup spilled; 0.5 with the tray lying flat on the table and at most 30 ml spilled, whether or not the bowl is on the placemat; 0.25 with the tray drawn wholly out in front of the lower shelf and at most 30 ml spilled; else 0.0. Spilled soup is whatever has left the bowl. In a real trial it is weighed: the bowl with its soup is weighed on a kitchen scale (1 g resolution) just before the trial; after the trial it is lifted straight up from where it ended, its outside and base are wiped dry, and it is weighed again. The loss in grams is the millilitres spilled (at most 10 g for 1.0, at most 30 g for 0.5 and 0.25). In simulation each bead whose centre has left the bowl's inside counts as 10 ml spilled: at most 1 of the 15 beads out for 1.0, and at most 3 for 0.5 and 0.25. The trial ends at the run limit, or once the full score has held with everything still for 1 s.
reset_notes: Nothing is consumed: put the beads back in the bowl, stand the bowl in the middle of the tray with its handle to the right, and slide the tray back onto the lower shelf, centred.
fidelity: Rigid-body simulation (Isaac Sim 6.1, PhysX, 20 Hz control). Simplified: the 150 ml of soup is 15 rigid 8 mm beads, 10 ml each, with the rest of its mass in the bowl's body; they roll and spill but do not slosh. The demo's pinch on the handle lets the bowl sag about 25 degrees; 150 ml stays in to 30. The bowl's wall is 20 flat panels; the pass is three blocks; friction is set (tray 0.5, bowl 0.6, beads 0.3). Cameras 1280 x 704 (Dream-1 sees 320 x 176).
